newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Return of Bulgaria grain swaps due in Oct/Nov.
newsitem.headline: Return of Bulgaria grain swaps due in Oct/Nov.

text.p: Bulgaria must return 100,000 tonnes of wheat to Poland between October 1 and November 30 in exchange for grain supplied under a government-to-government deal in March, an agriculture ministry official said on Monday.
Bulgaria agreed the grain swap in February to combat an acute shortage caused by uncontrolled exports two years ago and a bad harvest last year.
Also, under two commercial contracts agreed with Swiss firm Glencore in March and May, Bulgaria must return a further 131,750 tonnes by November 1 in exchange for 100,000 tonnes imported.

The ministry last month forecast a wheat harvest of 2.4 million tonnes this year, but the new crop has been affected by hail in the past two weeks and the harvest, expected to start next month, may now be lower, the official said.
Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said in May Bulgaria needed to import 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat before next year's crop.
The government will impose a temporary 15 percent grain export tax to offset further grain imports.
